Consider the category of topological spaces <MATH_0001>.
There is a natural faithful functor <MATH_0002>
which commutes with products and equalizers. But it does
not reflect isomorphisms. And, in fact it turns out that
the analogue of Lemma <REF_0001> is wrong.
Namely, suppose <MATH_0003> with the discrete
topology. Let <MATH_0004>, for <MATH_0005> be a discrete
topological space. For any subset <MATH_0006>
define <MATH_0007> with the
discrete topology. Then this is a presheaf of topological
spaces whose underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf, see
Example <REF_0002>.
However, if each <MATH_0008> has at least two elements, then
this is not a sheaf of topological spaces
according to Definition <REF_0003>.
The reader may check that putting the <TEXTITOPEN_0001>product topology<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> on
each <MATH_0009> does lead to a sheaf
of topological spaces over <MATH_0010>.
